values.label: Urine output
values.where: Chapter 25, The Body Fluid Compartments: Table 25-1, Daily Intake and Output of Water (urine, normal conditions: 1400 mL/day)
values.note: Single typical value under normal conditions; it varies widely with what you drink.

values.label: Sodium taken back: proximal tubule
values.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology, 'Sodium Balance': Figure 6.19, handling of Na+ in the nephron (the proximal tubule reabsorbs 67% of the filtered load)

values.label: Sodium taken back: thick ascending limb
values.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology, 'Sodium Balance': Figure 6.19, handling of Na+ in the nephron (the thick ascending limb reabsorbs 25% of the filtered load)

values.label: Sodium taken back: early distal tubule
values.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology, 'Sodium Balance': Figure 6.19, handling of Na+ in the nephron (the early distal tubule reabsorbs 5% of the filtered load)

values.label: Sodium taken back: late distal tubule and collecting duct
values.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology, 'Sodium Balance': Figure 6.19, handling of Na+ in the nephron (the late distal tubule and collecting duct reabsorb 3% of the filtered load)
values.note: The model lumps the late distal tubule with the collecting duct, as the source does.

values.label: Sodium excreted in urine
values.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology, 'Sodium Balance': Figure 6.19, handling of Na+ in the nephron (less than 1% of the filtered load is excreted)
values.note: The source gives only an upper limit: less than 1%.

values.label: Plasma potassium
values.where: Chapter 1, Functional Organization of the Human Body and Control of the 'Internal Environment': Table 1-1, Important Constituents and Physical Characteristics of Extracellular Fluid (potassium ion: normal value 4.2, normal range 3.8 to 5.0 mmol/L)

values.label: Plasma bicarbonate
values.where: Chapter 1: Table 1-1, Important Constituents and Physical Characteristics of Extracellular Fluid (bicarbonate ion: normal value 24, normal range 24 to 32 mmol/L)
values.note: The table's normal value sits at the bottom of its own range.

states.label: Loop diuretic (furosemide)
states.summary: Inhibits Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransport in the thick ascending limb, so less sodium is reabsorbed there.
states.context: Directions are listed only where a cited location supports them: sodium taken back in the thick ascending limb (its transport mechanism), plasma potassium (Potassium Balance) and plasma bicarbonate (contraction alkalosis, Chapter 7). The bicarbonate rise is not a direct effect of the transport block: it follows the loss of extracellular volume. Urine output and sodium excreted are not given a sourced direction here, though the model shows both rising.
states.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology: Table 6.7, Summary of the Functions of the Major Nephron Segments, p. 278 (thick ascending limb: Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransport); 'Potassium Balance', p. 295 (loop diuretics and K+ secretion); Chapter 7, Acid-Base Physiology: contraction alkalosis, Table 7.5, p. 331

states.label: Thiazide diuretic
states.summary: Inhibits Na+-Cl− cotransport in the early distal tubule, so less sodium is reabsorbed there.
states.context: Directions are listed only where a cited location supports them: sodium taken back in the early distal tubule (its transport mechanism), plasma potassium (Potassium Balance) and plasma bicarbonate (contraction alkalosis, Chapter 7). The bicarbonate rise is not a direct effect of the transport block: it follows the loss of extracellular volume. Urine output and sodium excreted are not given a sourced direction here, though the model shows both rising.
states.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology: Table 6.7, Summary of the Functions of the Major Nephron Segments, p. 278 (early distal tubule: Na+-Cl− cotransport); 'Potassium Balance', p. 295 (thiazide diuretics and K+ secretion); Chapter 7, Acid-Base Physiology: contraction alkalosis, Table 7.5, p. 331

states.label: Potassium-sparing diuretic
states.summary: Opposes aldosterone's action on sodium reabsorption in the late distal tubule and collecting duct, so less sodium is reabsorbed there and less potassium is secreted.
states.context: Directions are listed only where a cited location supports them: sodium taken back in the late distal tubule and collecting duct (their transport mechanism) and plasma potassium (Potassium Balance). Urine output, sodium excreted and bicarbonate are not given a sourced direction here.
states.where: Chapter 6, Renal Physiology: Table 6.7, Summary of the Functions of the Major Nephron Segments, p. 278 (late distal tubule and collecting duct principal cells: aldosterone-dependent Na+ reabsorption and K+ secretion); 'Potassium Balance', p. 295 (potassium-sparing diuretics and K+ secretion)
